prerequisites: Basic knowledge of algebra, analysis, physics, and electrical networks from semester 1 and 2 of the first phase of the bachelor's program in engineering sciences.

learning_outcomes.text: Gain insight into both the theoretical and practical building blocks of information transfer and processing.
Understand the physical principles behind signal transfer.
Be able to make qualitative and quantitative statements about signal transfer.
Master the Fourier transform for time-dependent signals.
Know the most important digital electronic building blocks.

syllabus_topics: Digital design and processing of binary information
Information sources: discrete information sources without and with memory
Processing and filtering of digital signals
Physical transmission channels via guided wave propagation and via radiation
Multiplexing: multiple transmission channels along the same physical channel
Discrete information sources and source coding
Physical transmission channels and baseband transmission

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

assessment_rules: The exam consists of exercise-type questions, potentially combining multiple aspects in one question. There are also elements to assess theoretical understanding. An extensive, structured formula sheet is provided during the exam.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
